name: Review Fleet Work and Improve
description: Operator-triggered improvement loop. Given an operator's description of something they just tried with the fleet, find the relevant recent missions, review what happened from the work tree, classify shortcomings into improvement modules, execute the improvements, and report back. Use when an operator asks Prime to review recent agent work and make it better.

request.description: The operator's description of what they tried and what to improve

target_agent.description: Which fleet agent/team to review, if named (e.g. dot, archie)

lookback_hours.description: How far back to search for the relevant missions

steps.title: Find the work to review
steps.description: The operator described something they just tried: ${request}. Using work-management, run work-log-read for the relevant window (--hours ${lookback_hours}; add --owner ${target_agent} if an agent was named). Identify the specific mission(s) that match the operator's description. If several match, pick the most recent that fits; if none clearly match, ask the operator to clarify which attempt they mean (needs_input).
steps.accept_criteria: The matching mission(s) identified by work ID, with a one-line summary of what each tried to do. If ambiguous, a clarifying question was asked instead of guessing.

steps.title: Review what happened (evidence from the work tree)
steps.description: ⚠️ READ-ONLY STEP. For each identified mission, read the full work tree via work-management (work-log-read / the mission tree). Derive the evidence DIRECTLY from the tree — do NOT rely on aggregated metrics that may not exist. Capture: total envelopes (M/C/T), failed or retried tasks, cortex re-plans (a checkpoint re-issued after a failure), delegation handoffs and their round-trip counts, any ENOENT/permission/access errors, time from start to finish, and where the mission stalled or produced a poor result. Optionally cross-reference brain-telemetry-read for dispatch failures on the same window.
steps.accept_criteria: A concrete assessment: what went wrong or was suboptimal, with specific evidence (envelope counts, failure points, round-trips, durations) cited from the work tree — not from assumed telemetry.

steps.title: Classify and improve
steps.description: Map the assessment to one or more of the 8 improvement modules (read the architect-prime project context for module definitions). For each module, follow its improvement process: p-improve-daemons, p-improve-souls, p-improve-context, p-improve-gateway, p-improve-work-layer, p-improve-skills, p-improve-dashboard, or p-improve-delegation. Execute the evidence→fix→verify cycle defined by that process. Keep each module's changes separate (one module per commit).
steps.accept_criteria: At least one module's improvement executed with before/after reasoning. Changed files or Firestore documents listed. Changes scoped one-module-per-commit.

steps.title: Submit changes
steps.description: For repo file changes (code, processes, SOULs, skills): using git-ops, create a branch 'improve/{module}-{short-desc}', commit, push, open a PR to main with what was improved, the module, the evidence, and expected effect. For data-only changes (project context, core memory, process/responsibility in Firestore): persist directly and record the document path. A change is one or the other.
steps.accept_criteria: PR link provided for code changes, OR Firestore document path(s) for data changes. One of the two is present for each improvement.

steps.title: Report back to the operator
steps.description: Reply in the operator's chat thread (the same dashboard conversation that triggered this). Summarize: which mission was reviewed, what was found (in plain language — the operator is not reading the work tree), what was improved, the PR link or Firestore change, and what the operator should expect to see differently next time. Keep it concise and non-technical.
steps.accept_criteria: A clear, concise summary delivered to the originating dashboard chat thread, understandable without opening the PR.
